plot01_hist_value.png.statistical_suitability: Histogram/KDE is statistically optimal for continuous univar distribution.
plot01_hist_value.png.axis_labeling_and_units: X: Valuation (USD Billions), Y: Franchise Frequency
plot01_hist_value.png.empirical_inference: The valuation distribution exhibits a strong positive (right) skew, with over 60% of top-50 teams clustered between $2.4B and $3.5B. A distinct elite tier (Cowboys, Yankees, Knicks) pulls the right tail above $5.0B, creating a notable gap between the median ($3.2B) and top performers.

plot02_box_value_sport.png.statistical_suitability: Boxplot+stripplot captures median, IQR, and dispersion per group.
plot02_box_value_sport.png.axis_labeling_and_units: X: Sport Discipline, Y: Valuation (USD Billions)
plot02_box_value_sport.png.empirical_inference: European Soccer maintains the highest median valuation (.10B) and mean valuation (.84B) due to exclusive global brand equity, while the NFL maintains the largest market share (52% of top 50, 26 teams) and a highly consistent valuation floor (median .07B, IQR .665B) anchored by collective media agreements and strict salary cap parity. Basketball exhibits the widest valuation dispersion (IQR .95B) between marquee big-market teams (.6B-.0B) and small-market franchises.

plot03_bar_top10.png.plot_type: Horizontal Bar Chart with Value Annotations
plot03_bar_top10.png.statistical_suitability: Horizontal bar chart provides clear ranking of top-N values.
plot03_bar_top10.png.axis_labeling_and_units: X: Valuation (USD Billions), Y: Team Name
plot03_bar_top10.png.empirical_inference: Dallas Cowboys claim the pinnacle ($5.70B), followed by New York Yankees ($5.25B) and New York Knicks ($5.00B). American franchises capture 7 of the top 10 positions, while European football giants Barcelona ($4.76B) and Real Madrid ($4.75B) anchor the global contingent.

plot04_donut_sport_share.png.statistical_suitability: Donut chart presents composition/market shares summing to 100%.
plot04_donut_sport_share.png.empirical_inference: American Football (NFL) accounts for an overwhelming 52.0% (26 of 50) of the globe's premier sports properties. Basketball (NBA) holds 18.0%, Soccer accounts for 18.0%, and Baseball (MLB) represents 12.0%, proving the commercial heft of US gridiron football.

plot05_scatter_price_vs_val.png.plot_type: Scatter Plot with OLS Regression Trendline
plot05_scatter_price_vs_val.png.statistical_suitability: Scatter+trendline captures bivariate capital gain relationship.
plot05_scatter_price_vs_val.png.axis_labeling_and_units: X: Initial Price Paid (USD Millions), Y: Current Valuation (USD Billions)
plot05_scatter_price_vs_val.png.empirical_inference: Franchises acquired at modest baseline prices (<$300M in the 20th century) show dramatic multi-thousand-percent capital gains. Newer transactions above $1.5B show contemporary institutional pricing, resulting in higher nominal capital outlays.

plot06_corr_heatmap.png.statistical_suitability: Heatmap with correlation coefficients shows pairwise linear dependencies.
plot06_corr_heatmap.png.empirical_inference: Years Held exhibits a strong negative correlation with Year Purchased (-1.00) and a moderate negative correlation with Price Paid (-0.57), verifying inflation and skyrocketing franchise values over successive ownership eras. Value correlates weakly with 5-year growth (-0.04), indicating mature market resilience.

plot07_violin_growth_sport.png.plot_type: Violin Plot with Embedded Quartile Markers
plot07_violin_growth_sport.png.statistical_suitability: Violin plot visualizes multimodal kernel densities and extreme tails.
plot07_violin_growth_sport.png.axis_labeling_and_units: X: Sport Discipline, Y: 5-Year Value Change (%)
plot07_violin_growth_sport.png.empirical_inference: Soccer and select NBA teams show wide, tall violin profiles with long tails extending past 150%-200% growth (e.g., PSG at 207%, Liverpool at 165%), driven by international branding. The NFL exhibits a compact bell distribution clustered tightly around 50%-65%.

plot08_pairplot.png.statistical_suitability: Pairplot illuminates pairwise clusters and class separability.
plot08_pairplot.png.empirical_inference: Bivariate distributions demonstrate distinct cluster boundaries: Soccer occupies the high-growth perimeter, MLB occupies moderate value and moderate acquisition prices, and NFL dominates the central high-density valuation core.

plot09_line_vintage_trend.png.statistical_suitability: Dual-axis line chart traces macroeconomic vintage trends over decades.
plot09_line_vintage_trend.png.axis_labeling_and_units: X: Acquisition Decade, Y1: Mean Value (), Y2: Mean 5-Yr Growth (%)
plot09_line_vintage_trend.png.empirical_inference: Franchises held since the 1920s-1970s maintain remarkably resilient multi-billion-dollar values. Meanwhile, franchises bought during the 2000s and 2010s show accelerated recent 5-year percentage valuation gains due to modernization and global streaming monetization.

plot10_qq_density.png.statistical_suitability: Q-Q + KDE provides theoretical and empirical test of Gaussian normality.
plot10_qq_density.png.axis_labeling_and_units: Left: Theoretical Quantiles vs Sample (), Right: Valuation () vs Density
plot10_qq_density.png.empirical_inference: The Q-Q plot exhibits pronounced convex curvature at upper quantiles, confirming heavy positive skewness. This violates standard Gaussian assumptions, strongly justifying nonparametric and tree-based data mining methods (such as FP-Growth and Naive Bayes discretization).

plot11_stacked_sport_country.png.plot_type: Stacked Bar Chart with Legend Breakdown
plot11_stacked_sport_country.png.statistical_suitability: Stacked bar chart captures cross-tabulation of discrete geographic segments.
plot11_stacked_sport_country.png.axis_labeling_and_units: X: Sport Discipline, Y: Franchise Count, Legend: Country
plot11_stacked_sport_country.png.empirical_inference: American Football, Baseball, and Basketball are 100% geographically concentrated in the USA. Conversely, the Soccer category is partitioned across the UK (5 teams), Spain (2 teams), Germany (1 team), and France (1 team), illustrating Europe's polycentric soccer landscape.

plot12_bubble_valuation.png.statistical_suitability: Bubble chart maps 3 continuous variables into 2D space + marker scale.
plot12_bubble_valuation.png.axis_labeling_and_units: X: 5-Yr Growth (%), Y: Value (), Size: Years Held (Years), Color: Value ()
plot12_bubble_valuation.png.empirical_inference: Franchises held for decades (largest bubbles) occupy the upper valuation plateau with steady compound gains. Outlying high-growth properties (e.g., Golden State Warriors, LA Rams, PSG) are medium-sized bubbles purchased in the modern era, capturing rapid franchise re-evaluations.

plot13_confusion_matrix_nb.png.plot_type: Confusion Matrix Heatmap with Tier Counts
plot13_confusion_matrix_nb.png.statistical_suitability: Confusion matrix reveals true positive and off-diagonal error distribution.
plot13_confusion_matrix_nb.png.axis_labeling_and_units: X: Predicted Tier, Y: Actual Tier, Values: Franchise Count
plot13_confusion_matrix_nb.png.empirical_inference: Under strict leak-free train/test evaluation (discretization and one-hot encoding fitted strictly on the 80% train split), Naive Bayes achieves 50.0% test accuracy and 0.5000 Macro F1 across High, Med, and Low tiers. Errors are confined to adjacent boundary classes, verifying sound probabilistic calibration.

plot14_agnes_dendrogram.png.plot_type: Hierarchical Dendrogram with Dissimilarity Cut Line
plot14_agnes_dendrogram.png.statistical_suitability: Dendrogram displays tree topology, merge distances, and cluster cutoff.
plot14_agnes_dendrogram.png.axis_labeling_and_units: X: Sports Franchise (League), Y: Ward Dissimilarity Distance
plot14_agnes_dendrogram.png.empirical_inference: With exact collinear tenure duplication pruned (r=-1.0 between Year_Purchased_Clean and Years_Held), AGNES clustering with Ward's linkage exhibits high cophenetic tree fidelity (0.7351) and validates k=3 as optimal (silhouette 0.3764), segregating Recent High-Capital Takeovers (7 teams), Hyper-Growth Outliers (4 teams), and Historic Blue-Chip Franchises (39 teams).

plot15_pyspark_speedup.png.variables_evaluated: Dataset Scale N x Execution Time & Speedup
plot15_pyspark_speedup.png.statistical_suitability: Dual-panel log-log curve and speedup bar chart illustrate Amdahl crossover.
plot15_pyspark_speedup.png.axis_labeling_and_units: Left: Records N vs Time (Seconds, Log Scale), Right: Scale Factor vs Speedup Ratio (x)
plot15_pyspark_speedup.png.empirical_inference: Empirical verification of distributed computing crossover dynamics: At 1x (N=50) and 10x (N=500), single-node Scikit-Learn outperforms PySpark (speedup 0.00x - 0.27x) due to JVM context initialization, Catalyst query planning, and RDD partition serialization overhead. However, between N=500 and N=5,000 (~1,800 records), computational workload crosses the parity threshold (1.0x). At 100x (N=5,000), PySpark achieves a 1.63x speedup, and at 1000x (N=50,000), it achieves a massive 5.20x speedup (13.82s vs 71.85s) by executing FP-Growth and Gaussian Naive Bayes across multi-core workers.
